tier_reason: C stands: first-party book figures; whether they predate the 2022 initialisation fix is unknown.

corrections.caveats: Enricher: commit ac595cb (2022-02-09, 'Fixed typo in initialization of the string') changed the 00_substring_sort_prep.C memset length from N to L; before it only 2^14 of the 2^18 bytes were initialised, so suffixes were not guaranteed to differ inside the buffer, and it is unknown whether the book's 98/210/74 ms came from pre-fix or post-fix code. Issue #2 (closed by its reporter, no numbers) is titled '04 slower than 03', so the direction of the effect is unconfirmed on other toolchains. compare() never stops at NUL, so it over-reads on equal strings at different addresses; 12_compare_mbm_c/d isolate signedness with a bound. No strcmp or memcmp baseline anywhere in Chapter02.

corrections.tradeoffs: The spinlock backs off with a 1 ns nanosleep after 8 failed spins (timer slack stretches it, 50 us by default on Linux); on a loaded or oversubscribed machine, or with a preempted lock holder, spinning wastes cores and can invert priorities. Not fair, not recursive, no try_lock (so it works with std::condition_variable_any only); no pause instruction and no padding on the flag. spinlock.h is POSIX-only (nanosleep) and rw_spinlock needs a 64-bit long, so it breaks on MSVC despite the README listing Windows.
corrections.caveats: Enricher: 02_stack.C reads state.thread_index and state.threads as data members, so it fails to build on Google Benchmark 1.6.0 and later (needs 1.5.x). Aggregate real-time items/s rewards unfairness (a thread that keeps re-acquiring the lock raises throughput).
